reason: The problem.txt contract requires abs(actual[i] - erf(x[i])) <= 1e-6 for every element over every finite FP16 value, with relative tolerance zero. An exhaustive runtime sweep of all 63,488 finite FP16 values (probe t8) shows the kernel's max absolute error vs exact FP64 erf is 1.2918e-6 at x≈0.5083, with 1,394 values exceeding the 1e-6 tolerance — a direct, in-scope contract violation. The decomposition probe confirms the cause is the truncated A&S coefficients (1.06141, -1.45315, 1.42141, -0.28450, 0.25483): the same formula in FP64 already violates on 1,060 values (max 1.0627e-6). Claim c2 (FP32 evaluation chain independently pushing error over budget) is rebutted by probe t9 (max evaluation-chain error 6.07e-7, never exceeding 1e-6). The FP16 domain is exhaustively enumerable, so this evidence is globally decisive for the stated contract. No open claims remain and the Skeptic recorded no new claims after reviewing all evidence.
